[engineering_lead]: # User Management REST API Design

## 1. Scope and principles

The API supports:

- User registration and authentication
- Email verification and password reset
- User profile management
- Administrative user management
- Role-based authorization
- Session and token management
- Pagination, filtering, sorting, and API versioning

Base URL:

```text
https://api.example.com/v1
```

All requests and responses use JSON unless otherwise stated.

---

## 2. Resource model

### User

```json
{
  "id": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "firstName": "Alex",
  "lastName": "Morgan",
  "status": "active",
  "roles": ["user"],
  "emailVerified": true,
  "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-01-20T14:05:00Z"
}
```

The API must never return:

- Password hashes
- Password reset tokens
- Refresh tokens
- Internal security metadata
- MFA secrets

### Roles

Initial roles:

- `user`: Manage their own profile and sessions
- `support`: Read users and assist with account operations
- `admin`: Create, update, disable, and assign roles
- `security_admin`: Manage authentication policies and revoke sessions globally

---

# 3. Authentication endpoints

## Register

```http
POST /v1/auth/register
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "password": "correct horse battery staple",
  "firstName": "Alex",
  "lastName": "Morgan"
}
```

Response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Location: /v1/users/usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2
```

```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
    "email": "alex@example.com",
    "firstName": "Alex",
    "lastName": "Morgan",
    "status": "pending_verification",
    "roles": ["user"],
    "emailVerified": false,
    "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "updatedAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
  },
  "message": "Check your email to verify your account."
}
```

For privacy, production systems may return the same response whether the email already exists.

---

## Login

```http
POST /v1/auth/login
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "password": "correct horse battery staple",
  "rememberMe": true
}
```

Response option using secure cookies:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: access_token=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
Set-Cookie: refresh_token=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/v1/auth
```

```json
{
  "user": {
    "id": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
    "email": "alex@example.com",
    "firstName": "Alex",
    "lastName": "Morgan",
    "status": "active",
    "roles": ["user"],
    "emailVerified": true
  },
  "expiresIn": 900
}
```

For non-browser clients, the API can return:

```json
{
  "accessToken": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
  "tokenType": "Bearer",
  "expiresIn": 900,
  "refreshToken": "opaque-refresh-token"
}
```

---

## Refresh an access token

```http
POST /v1/auth/refresh
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "refreshToken": "opaque-refresh-token"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "accessToken": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
  "tokenType": "Bearer",
  "expiresIn": 900
}
```

Refresh tokens should be rotated on every use. Reuse of a revoked refresh token should revoke the entire token family.

---

## Logout current session

```http
POST /v1/auth/logout
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

The server revokes the associated refresh token and clears authentication cookies.

---

## Logout all sessions

```http
POST /v1/auth/logout-all
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Requires the user to reauthenticate or provide a recent MFA challenge for high-risk accounts.

```http
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

---

## Get the current user

```http
GET /v1/auth/me
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Response:

```json
{
  "id": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "firstName": "Alex",
  "lastName": "Morgan",
  "status": "active",
  "roles": ["user"],
  "emailVerified": true
}
```

---

## Request a password reset

```http
POST /v1/auth/password-reset/request
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "email": "alex@example.com"
}
```

The response must not disclose whether the account exists:

```json
{
  "message": "If an account exists, password reset instructions will be sent."
}
```

---

## Complete a password reset

```http
POST /v1/auth/password-reset/complete
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "token": "single-use-reset-token",
  "newPassword": "new correct horse battery staple"
}
```

Response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

All active sessions should be revoked after a successful password reset.

---

## Verify an email address

```http
POST /v1/auth/email-verification/verify
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "token": "single-use-email-verification-token"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "message": "Email address verified successfully."
}
```

Resend verification:

```http
POST /v1/auth/email-verification/resend
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

---

# 4. User resource endpoints

## Get a user

```http
GET /v1/users/{userId}
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Authorization rules:

- Users may retrieve their own profile
- `support` and `admin` may retrieve users according to policy
- Sensitive fields should be restricted to privileged roles

---

## Update the current user

```http
PATCH /v1/users/me
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "firstName": "Alexandra",
  "lastName": "Morgan"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "id": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "firstName": "Alexandra",
  "lastName": "Morgan",
  "status": "active",
  "roles": ["user"],
  "emailVerified": true,
  "updatedAt": "2025-01-20T14:05:00Z"
}
```

Email changes should require confirmation of the new email address and, preferably, recent authentication.

---

## Delete or deactivate the current account

```http
DELETE /v1/users/me
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Recommended behavior:

- Soft-delete the account
- Revoke all sessions
- Anonymize or retain data according to legal and retention requirements
- Return `204 No Content`

Administrative deletion:

```http
DELETE /v1/users/{userId}
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
```

This should require an explicit reason and generate an audit event.

---

# 5. Administrative endpoints

## List users

```http
GET /v1/users
Authorization: Bearer <admin-or-support-token>
```

Supported query parameters:

```text
?limit=25
&cursor=eyJpZCI6InVzcl8...
&status=active
&role=user
&emailVerified=true
&search=alex
&sort=-createdAt
```

Response:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
      "email": "alex@example.com",
      "firstName": "Alex",
      "lastName": "Morgan",
      "status": "active",
      "roles": ["user"],
      "emailVerified": true,
      "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "limit": 25,
    "nextCursor": "eyJpZCI6InVzcl8...",
    "hasMore": true
  }
}
```

Use cursor-based pagination for production endpoints. Enforce a maximum `limit`, such as `100`.

---

## Update a user as an administrator

```http
PATCH /v1/users/{userId}
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json
```

Request:

```json
{
  "status": "suspended",
  "roles": ["user"],
  "suspensionReason": "Repeated policy violations"
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "id": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "status": "suspended",
  "roles": ["user"],
  "updatedAt": "2025-01-20T15:00:00Z"
}
```

Protect role changes with:

- Admin-only authorization
- Audit logging
- Optional dual approval for privileged roles
- Prevention of accidental removal of the last administrator

---

## List a user’s sessions

```http
GET /v1/users/me/sessions
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Response:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "ses_01HZ...",
      "device": "Chrome on macOS",
      "ipAddress": "203.0.113.10",
      "createdAt": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
      "lastUsedAt": "2025-01-20T14:10:00Z",
      "current": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Do not expose raw token values.

Revoke a session:

```http
DELETE /v1/users/me/sessions/{sessionId}
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

---

# 6. Validation rules

## Email

- Required during registration
- Normalize domain casing
- Store a canonical representation
- Validate syntax and maximum length
- Enforce uniqueness using a database constraint
- Do not rely only on application-level uniqueness checks

## Names

- UTF-8 supported
- Maximum length, for example 100 characters
- Reject control characters
- Trim leading and trailing whitespace

## Passwords

Recommended rules:

- Minimum length: 12 characters
- Maximum length: at least 128 characters
- Accept spaces and Unicode
- Do not require arbitrary composition rules
- Reject known breached passwords using a breach-password service or local corpus
- Never log or persist plaintext passwords

Example validation response:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/problems/validation-error",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "detail": "One or more fields are invalid.",
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "password",
      "code": "PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT",
      "message": "Password must contain at least 12 characters."
    }
  ],
  "requestId": "req_01HZ..."
}
```

---

# 7. Password handling

Use Argon2id with parameters calibrated for the production environment.

Example conceptual configuration:

```text
algorithm: Argon2id
memory: 64 MiB or higher
iterations: 3+
parallelism: 1–4
salt: unique random salt per password
```

Example server-side pseudocode:

```python
from argon2 import PasswordHasher

password_hasher = PasswordHasher(
    time_cost=3,
    memory_cost=65536,
    parallelism=2
)

password_hash = password_hasher.hash(plain_password)

try:
    password_hasher.verify(password_hash, submitted_password)
except VerifyMismatchError:
    raise InvalidCredentials()
```

Additional controls:

- Rehash passwords when parameters become outdated
- Use constant-time comparison where applicable
- Rate-limit login and password reset attempts
- Revoke sessions after password changes
- Never send passwords by email
- Never include credentials in URLs

---

# 8. Token and session strategy

## Recommended approach

For browser applications:

- Short-lived access token: 10–15 minutes
- Secure, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` cookies
- Opaque, rotating refresh token
- Server-side refresh-token persistence
- Refresh-token family tracking and reuse detection

For APIs and native clients:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Access tokens may be JWTs containing only minimal claims:

```json
{
  "iss": "https://api.example.com",
  "sub": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
  "aud": "user-management-api",
  "jti": "tok_01HZ...",
  "iat": 1736951400,
  "exp": 1736952300,
  "roles": ["user"]
}
```

Recommendations:

- Sign JWTs with an asymmetric algorithm such as RS256 or EdDSA
- Publish public keys through a JWKS endpoint
- Rotate signing keys
- Validate issuer, audience, expiration, signature, and token ID
- Do not place sensitive information in JWT claims
- Keep authorization decisions server-side for high-risk operations

A session record may contain:

```text
id
user_id
refresh_token_hash
token_family_id
device_metadata
ip_address
created_at
last_used_at
expires_at
revoked_at
```

Store only hashes of opaque refresh tokens.

---

# 9. Authorization

Use role-based access control combined with resource ownership checks.

Example policy:

| Operation | User | Support | Admin | Security Admin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Read own profile | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Update own profile | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| List users | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Suspend users | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Assign roles | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Revoke all sessions | Own only | No | Yes | Yes |
| Change authentication policy | No | No | No | Yes |

Authorization middleware example:

```typescript
function requireRole(...allowedRoles: string[]) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    const hasRole = req.user.roles.some((role: string) =>
      allowedRoles.includes(role)
    );

    if (!hasRole) {
      return next(new ForbiddenError());
    }

    next();
  };
}
```

Every endpoint should also verify that the requested resource belongs to the authenticated user where applicable.

---

# 10. Error format

Use an RFC 9457/RFC 7807-style problem response.

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/problems/invalid-credentials",
  "title": "Invalid credentials",
  "status": 401,
  "code": "INVALID_CREDENTIALS",
  "detail": "The email or password is incorrect.",
  "requestId": "req_01HZ..."
}
```

Standard status codes:

- `400 Bad Request`: Malformed request
- `401 Unauthorized`: Missing or invalid authentication
- `403 Forbidden`: Authenticated but not authorized
- `404 Not Found`: Resource does not exist
- `409 Conflict`: State or uniqueness conflict
- `422 Unprocessable Entity`: Validation failure
- `429 Too Many Requests`: Rate limit exceeded
- `500 Internal Server Error`: Unexpected server failure

Avoid exposing whether an email exists in login, registration, and password-reset flows.

---

# 11. Security controls

## Transport and headers

- TLS 1.2 or later
- HSTS
- Secure and HttpOnly cookies
- `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict`
- Content Security Policy for web clients
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- Strict CORS allowlist
- No credentials in query parameters

## Abuse prevention

- Rate-limit login by IP and account identifier
- Rate-limit registration and password reset
- Progressive delays or temporary lockouts
- CAPTCHA or step-up verification after suspicious activity
- Detect credential stuffing and impossible travel
- Use generic authentication error messages

## CSRF

If cookies are used:

- Use SameSite cookies
- Add CSRF tokens for state-changing requests
- Validate the `Origin` header
- Do not permit overly broad CORS

## Auditing and monitoring

Audit:

- Login success and failure
- Password changes and resets
- Email changes
- Role changes
- Account suspension and deletion
- Session creation and revocation
- Administrative access

Audit records should include:

```json
{
  "event": "user.role_changed",
  "actorId": "usr_admin",
  "targetUserId": "usr_01HZ...",
  "metadata": {
    "oldRoles": ["user"],
    "newRoles": ["support"]
  },
  "ipAddress": "203.0.113.10",
  "occurredAt": "2025-01-20T15:00:00Z"
}
```

Do not log passwords, tokens, or full authorization headers.

---

# 12. Data model

Example relational schema:

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    email TEXT NOT NULL,
    email_normalized TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    first_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN (
        'pending_verification',
        'active',
        'suspended',
        'deleted'
    )),
    email_verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE TABLE user_roles (
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    role TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, role)
);

CREATE TABLE sessions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    refresh_token_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    token_family_id UUID NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE TABLE audit_events (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    actor_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    target_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    metadata JSONB,
    ip_address INET,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);
```

Use database indexes for:

- `email_normalized`
- `status`
- `created_at`
- `user_roles.role`
- Cursor-pagination fields

---

# 13. Versioning and compatibility

Use URL-based major versioning:

```text
/v1/users
/v2/users
```

Rules:

- Backward-compatible fields may be added without a version change
- Do not rename or remove fields in an existing major version
- Deprecate endpoints using the `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers
- Publish an OpenAPI document for every supported version
- Maintain contract and integration tests
- Announce breaking changes before sunset

Example:

```http
Deprecation: true
Sunset: Wed, 31 Dec 2025 23:59:59 GMT
Link: </v2/users>; rel="successor-version"
```

---


Response:

```http
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```

The server revokes the associated refresh token and clears authentication cookies.

### Logout all sessions

```http
POST /v1/auth/logout-all
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Requires reauthentication or, for high-risk accounts, a recent MFA challenge.


## 6. Validation rules

### Email

- Required during registration
- Normalize domain casing
- Store a canonical representation
- Validate syntax and maximum length
- Enforce uniqueness using a database constraint
- Do not rely only on application-level uniqueness checks

### Names

- Support UTF-8
- Maximum length, for example 100 characters
- Reject control characters
- Trim leading and trailing whitespace

### Passwords

Recommended rules:

- Minimum length: 12 characters
- Maximum length: at least 128 characters
- Accept spaces and Unicode
- Do not require arbitrary composition rules
- Reject known breached passwords using a breach-password service or local corpus
- Never log or persist plaintext passwords

Example validation response:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/problems/validation-error",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "detail": "One or more fields are invalid.",
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "password",
      "code": "PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT",
      "message": "Password must contain at least 12 characters."
    }
  ],
  "requestId": "req_01HZ..."
}
```

---

## 7. Password handling

Use Argon2id with parameters calibrated for the production environment.

Example configuration:

```text
algorithm: Argon2id
memory: 64 MiB or higher
iterations: 3+
parallelism: 1–4
salt: unique random salt per password
```

Example server-side pseudocode:

```python
from argon2 import PasswordHasher

password_hasher = PasswordHasher(
    time_cost=3,
    memory_cost=65536,
    parallelism=2
)

password_hash = password_hasher.hash(plain_password)

try:
    password_hasher.verify(password_hash, submitted_password)
except VerifyMismatchError:
    raise InvalidCredentials()
```

Additional controls:

- Rehash passwords when parameters become outdated
- Use constant-time comparison where applicable
- Rate-limit login and password reset attempts
- Revoke sessions after password changes
- Never send passwords by email
- Never include credentials in URLs

---

## 8. Token and session strategy

### Browser applications

Use:

- Short-lived access tokens: 10–15 minutes
- Secure, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` cookies
- Opaque, rotating refresh tokens
- Server-side refresh-token persistence
- Refresh-token family tracking and reuse detection

### APIs and native clients

Use:

```http
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
```

Access tokens may be JWTs containing only minimal claims:

```json
{
  "iss": "https://api.example.com",
  "sub": "usr_01HZX8Y7K3N4Q2",
  "aud": "user-management-api",
  "jti": "tok_01HZ...",
  "iat": 1736951400,
  "exp": 1736952300,
  "roles": ["user"]
}
```

Recommendations:

- Sign JWTs with an asymmetric algorithm such as RS256 or EdDSA
- Publish public keys through a JWKS endpoint
- Rotate signing keys
- Validate issuer, audience, expiration, signature, and token ID
- Do not place sensitive information in JWT claims
- Keep authorization decisions server-side for high-risk operations

A session record may contain:

```text
id
user_id
refresh_token_hash
token_family_id
device_metadata
ip_address
created_at
last_used_at
expires_at
revoked_at
```

Store only hashes of opaque refresh tokens.

## 9. Authorization

Use role-based access control combined with resource ownership checks.

| Operation | User | Support | Admin | Security Admin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Read own profile | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Update own profile | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| List users | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Suspend users | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Assign roles | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Revoke all sessions | Own only | No | Yes | Yes |
| Change authentication policy | No | No | No | Yes |

Authorization middleware example:

```typescript
function requireRole(...allowedRoles: string[]) {
  return (req, res, next) => {
    const hasRole = req.user.roles.some((role: string) =>
      allowedRoles.includes(role)
    );

    if (!hasRole) {
      return next(new ForbiddenError());
    }

    next();
  };
}
```

Every endpoint should also verify that the requested resource belongs to the authenticated user where applicable.

---

## 10. Error format

Use an RFC 9457/RFC 7807-style problem response:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/problems/invalid-credentials",
  "title": "Invalid credentials",
  "status": 401,
  "code": "INVALID_CREDENTIALS",
  "detail": "The email or password is incorrect.",
  "requestId": "req_01HZ..."
}
```

Standard status codes:

- `400 Bad Request`: Malformed request
- `401 Unauthorized`: Missing or invalid authentication
- `403 Forbidden`: Authenticated but not authorized
- `404 Not Found`: Resource does not exist
- `409 Conflict`: State or uniqueness conflict
- `422 Unprocessable Entity`: Validation failure
- `429 Too Many Requests`: Rate limit exceeded
- `500 Internal Server Error`: Unexpected server failure

Avoid exposing whether an email exists in login, registration, and password-reset flows.

---

## 11. Security controls

### Transport and headers

- TLS 1.2 or later
- HSTS
- Secure and HttpOnly cookies
- `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict`
- Content Security Policy for web clients
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- Strict CORS allowlist
- No credentials in query parameters

### Abuse prevention

- Rate-limit login by IP and account identifier
- Rate-limit registration and password reset
- Progressive delays or temporary lockouts
- CAPTCHA or step-up verification after suspicious activity
- Detect credential stuffing and impossible travel
- Use generic authentication error messages

### CSRF

If cookies are used:

- Use SameSite cookies
- Add CSRF tokens for state-changing requests
- Validate the `Origin` header
- Do not permit overly broad CORS

### Auditing and monitoring

Audit:

- Login success and failure
- Password changes and resets
- Email changes
- Role changes
- Account suspension and deletion
- Session creation and revocation
- Administrative access

Audit records should include:

```json
{
  "event": "user.role_changed",
  "actorId": "usr_admin",
  "targetUserId": "usr_01HZ...",
  "metadata": {
    "oldRoles": ["user"],
    "newRoles": ["support"]
  },
  "ipAddress": "203.0.113.10",
  "occurredAt": "2025-01-20T15:00:00Z"
}
```

Do not log passwords, tokens, or full authorization headers.

## 12. Data model

Example relational schema:

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    email TEXT NOT NULL,
    email_normalized TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    first_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN (
        'pending_verification',
        'active',
        'suspended',
        'deleted'
    )),
    email_verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE TABLE user_roles (
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    role TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, role)
);

CREATE TABLE sessions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    refresh_token_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    token_family_id UUID NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    last_used_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE TABLE audit_events (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    actor_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    target_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    metadata JSONB,
    ip_address INET,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);
```

Use database indexes for:

- `email_normalized`
- `status`
- `created_at`
- `user_roles.role`
- Cursor-pagination fields

## 13. Versioning and compatibility

Use URL-based major versioning:

```text
/v1/users
/v2/users
```

Rules:

- Backward-compatible fields may be added without a version change
- Do not rename or remove fields in an existing major version
- Deprecate endpoints using the `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers
- Publish an OpenAPI document for every supported version
- Maintain contract and integration tests
- Announce breaking changes before sunset

Example:

```http
Deprecation: true
Sunset: Wed, 31 Dec 2025 23:59:59 GMT
Link: </v2/users>; rel="successor-version"
```

Targets should be finalized using existing channel benchmarks. A reasonable launch scorecard could include:

- 25–35% email open rate
- 3–8% email click-through rate
- 30% webinar registration-to-attendance rate
- 20% documentation visitor-to-signup conversion
- 40% signup-to-first successful API request
- 25% first-request-to-second-session workflow completion

---

## 11. Engineering assets required

### Essential launch assets

- Versioned OpenAPI specification
- Interactive API reference
- Quick-start guide
- Authentication flow diagram
- Refresh-token rotation diagram
- RBAC permission matrix
- Error-response reference
- Postman or Insomnia collection
- cURL examples
- Sample applications in at least two supported languages
- Webhook or email-flow documentation, if applicable
- Security implementation guide
- Changelog and versioning policy
- FAQ and troubleshooting guide

### Recommended sample projects

- Browser application using secure cookies
- Native or server-to-server client using bearer tokens
- Admin dashboard demonstrating user search and role management
- Session-management example showing device revocation
- Password-reset and email-verification flow

### Required technical review

Before publishing, engineering should verify:

- Examples use safe placeholder credentials
- No real tokens or sensitive data appear in documentation
- Endpoint names and payloads match the deployed API
- Role permissions are accurately represented
- Security claims are supported by implementation
- Rate limits and token lifetimes are documented
- Deprecated endpoints and version policies are clearly identified

---

## 12. Campaign calls to action

### Primary CTA

**Start building with the User Management API**

### Supporting CTA

**Read the developer documentation**

### Demo CTA

**See secure authentication and session management in action**

### Final campaign message

**Your application deserves more than a login endpoint. Build the complete user lifecycle with secure authentication, clear authorization, manageable sessions, and REST APIs your developers can use with confidence.**
Please continue where you left off.
